facts.text: On the burned lower slope, flagging tape and cairns can pull you onto a worse side path; if you find yourself bushwhacking you are off the real trail, so back up to the climber's-right line over the logs (reports from July and August).
Marmots and other critters at the Lake Constance camp steal small items such as socks left in boots (August).
The gully up to the south col has about 200 ft of unavoidable rockfall exposure; stay clear of the fall line and avoid stopping in constrictions (late August).
By late August the only snow met was a short patch in the east-west notch, and snow gear went unused by parties that carried it.
In early July most Avalanche Canyon snow has melted, leaving a few easy snowfields between scree stretches.
In early June snow is continuous above the lake and soft enough that some parties managed without axe or crampons, though the runouts are poor.
At the summit block the easier line goes left, with good hand and footholds; a rap station sits on top if you prefer not to downclimb (July and August).
Gaiters help on the scree descent from the notch, which parties ski down in loose boulders; keep a group spread out.
